questions.q: Why is referencing a container image by digest (`@sha256:...`) more reproducible than referencing it by tag (`:latest` or `:v3`)?
options: Digests load faster than tags
Tags can be silently overwritten to point at a different image later; a digest cannot change
Tags are only supported by Kubeflow, not Airflow
There is no real difference
questions.explain: A tag can be reassigned to a new image at any time, so "the same tag" may not mean "the same image" later. A digest is a content hash and cannot be silently changed.

questions.q: Why does querying "the current state of the table" break reproducibility, compared to using a dataset snapshot?
options: Queries are slower than reading a file
A live table's contents change over time, so re-running the same query later can return different data
SQL cannot be used inside a pipeline task
Snapshots are always smaller than live tables
questions.explain: A live table changes as new data arrives, so the same query run at two different times can return different rows. A versioned snapshot or content hash stays fixed.

questions.q: In the guide's reproducible training task, what is the purpose of `mlflow.log_params(config)` combined with logging the git SHA?
options: To speed up training
To capture the full hyperparameter configuration and exact code version together, so the run can be recovered and understood later
To seed the random number generator
To register the model automatically regardless of quality
questions.explain: Logging the full config object and the git commit SHA together captures exactly which code and which settings produced a given run — two of the five reproducibility commitments.

questions.q: Where should a model quality gate (e.g. requiring AUC above a threshold before registration) live?
options: As a manual check a human performs before clicking "promote" in a dashboard
As code inside the pipeline step itself, evaluated automatically on every run
It isn't necessary if the training code is well tested
Only in a separate pipeline that runs once a quarter
questions.explain: The quality gate needs to be automated code inside the pipeline step so it is enforced consistently on every run, rather than depending on a human remembering to check.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five concrete reproducibility commitments described in this lesson?
options: Fixed random seeds
Versioned, immutable input data
Captured code version (git SHA)
Running the pipeline on the fastest available hardware
questions.explain: Hardware speed has nothing to do with reproducibility. The five commitments are pinned dependencies, fixed seeds, versioned data, captured code version, and captured config.
